stories.summary: Godrej Properties has acquired a 31-acre land parcel in Indore for approximately 130 crore rupees to develop a residential plotted project. The company plans a saleable area of 0.7 million square feet, marking its third project in the city. Expansion continues in high-growth housing markets.

stories.title: ORA Land sells out first phase of Karjat project
stories.summary: ORA Land has sold 150 plots in the first phase of its BluBay development in Karjat, generating over 145 crore rupees in revenue. The company announced the sellout at an event featuring brand ambassador Suryakumar Yadav. The project marks the group's entry into the plotted development segment.

stories.title: UP RERA mandates homebuyer consent for project changes
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority now requires promoters to obtain written consent from at least two-thirds of allottees before changing sanctioned project plans. Promoters must disclose the impact on carpet areas and common spaces. Changes are no longer a unilateral decision.

stories.title: Telangana regulator orders developer refunds
stories.summary: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has ordered developers to refund 60.22 lakh rupees plus 10.85 percent annual interest following complaints regarding missing flats and incomplete amenities. The regulator also imposed a 20.05 lakh rupee penalty on a separate firm. Possession remains a variable.

stories.title: Rera dismisses Joyville AOA plea
stories.summary: Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has dismissed a complaint regarding the maintenance handover of the Joyville housing project. Chairman Arun Kumar ruled that disputes between rival residents associations fall under the jurisdiction of the Registrar of Societies. The authority has left the matter to the registrar.

stories.title: Tenant ignores Supreme Court eviction order
stories.summary: A tenant has continued to occupy a property despite a Supreme Court eviction order. The tenant's son subsequently sold a share of the landlord's property to third parties, who then filed a suit against the landlord. The Madras High Court has struck the case off.

stories.title: Danube sells out Shahrukhz Residences
stories.summary: Danube Properties has sold out all penthouses at its Shahrukhz Residences project in Dubai on launch day. The waterfront units, designed by Gauri Khan, were priced at 50 crore rupees each. The project is named after actor Shah Rukh Khan, who attended the launch event.

stories.summary: Shorenstein Investment Advisers has acquired International Plaza 3, a 356,000-square-foot office tower in Dallas. The 13-story building recently underwent renovations including lobby and fitness center upgrades. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. This marks the firm's fifth acquisition in the city since 2024.

stories.title: Hyderabad office market grows as rents rise
stories.summary: Hyderabad leased 13.1 million square feet of office space through September 2026, a 50 percent increase from the previous year. Average rents rose 9 percent to 82 rupees per square foot. As the market tightens, some founders are now considering virtual offices to manage costs.

stories.title: Central Region office rents rise
stories.summary: Office rents in the Central Region rose 0.8 percent in the third quarter of 2026, according to Realion Research. Demand for premium spaces in Marina Bay and Raffles Place drove the growth. Overall office stock in the region fell by 72,000 square feet during the period.

stories.title: Fab India opens Raipur store
stories.summary: Fab India has opened a new store at Ambuja Mall in Raipur. The retail platform, founded by John Bissell, now operates 342 domestic stores across India. The brand offers ethnic and fusion wear alongside home and personal care products, targeting a growing market for ethnic apparel.

stories.title: Brandman Retail plans expansion
stories.summary: Brandman Retail aims to reach 50 stores by March 2027. The company, which distributes international sportswear and lifestyle brands, reported 162.41 crore rupees in revenue for fiscal year 2026. Growth is driven by an expanded retail network and the company's exclusive brand outlets.

stories.title: CBI registers fraud case against Kishore Biyani
stories.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation has registered an FIR against Kishore Biyani and Future Retail Ltd for an alleged bank fraud of 904.32 crore rupees. Biyani, once a prominent figure in Indian retail, previously expressed ambitions to join the pantheon of global business leaders.

stories.title: CBRE on data center land demand
stories.summary: CBRE senior vice president Brian Pankratz says data center developers are competing for land with sufficient power infrastructure and municipal approval. Zoning restrictions and moratoriums are increasingly shaping site searches as demand for computing capacity grows, tightening the supply of suitable development locations.

stories.title: India warehousing leasing rises
stories.summary: India's warehousing market recorded 19.1 million square feet of leasing in the third quarter of 2026, a 12 percent year-on-year increase. Manufacturing and third-party logistics operators accounted for 76 percent of demand. Occupiers continue to show a preference for Grade A facilities.

stories.title: Foropoint buys Corona industrial building
stories.summary: Foropoint has purchased a 117,000-square-foot industrial facility in Corona for 21.5 million dollars. The property is fully leased to a tenant serving the aerospace, automotive and medical industries. The building features 27-foot to 29-foot clear heights and 222 parking stalls.

stories.title: Sutton officials defend data center proposal
stories.summary: Sutton officials are proceeding with a proposed data center project despite criticism from residents. The town stated it is evaluating opportunities to strengthen its financial future. The project involves two companies owned by the Kraft family, which have faced significant public opposition.

stories.title: ReNew Energy plans 80,000 crore investment in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: ReNew Energy has proposed an 80,000 crore rupee investment in Andhra Pradesh for digital and clean energy projects. The plan includes a 1 GW hyperscale data center, polysilicon production, and a technical excellence center. The company aims to broaden its footprint through these renewable-powered infrastructure ventures.

stories.title: Georgia warehouses listed for sale after detention center plans cancelled
stories.summary: Federal officials have cancelled plans to convert two large Georgia warehouses into immigration detention centers following public and political opposition. The properties are now listed for sale. The proposal for the Lithia Springs site had previously drawn criticism for its potential to hold 10,000 people.

stories.title: Georgia towns opposed plans to turn two huge warehouses into ICE detention centers, including one designed for up to 10,
stories.summary: Federal officials have officially cancelled plans to turn two large warehouses in Georgia into immigration detention centres. Both properties have now been listed for sale following strong public and political opposition. The decision is a major win for local communities in Douglas and Jackson counties,

stories.title: Cabinet approves 2,390 crore for Noida Metro expansion
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved 2,390 crore rupees for the Noida Metro Aqua Line extension. The 8.4-kilometer project will connect Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4 with five new elevated stations. The expansion aims to improve urban mobility and reduce road congestion in the region.

stories.title: Aqua Line Metro Extension to Greater Noida Sector 4 Approved
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday, Nov. 11, approved the Aqua Line Metro Extension from Noida’s Sector 51 to Greater Noida’s Sector 4. The 8.449-kilometer corridor is part of the Noida Metro Rail Project and will have five elevated stations.

stories.title: Bengaluru Metro Pink Line set for inauguration
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the 7.5-km elevated section of Bengaluru's Pink Line on November 14. The launch will bring the city's operational network to 103.6 km. The project opens to the public following years of missed deadlines.

stories.title: Trial runs begin on Bengaluru Metro Phase 2A and 2B
stories.summary: Trial runs have commenced on the Byappanahalli to KR Puram stretch of the Bengaluru Metro. The Phase 2A corridor is expected to be operational by mid 2027, with the Phase 2B airport corridor following in March 2028. The two projects carry a combined estimated cost of 80.48 billion rupees.

stories.title: India and Norway discuss waste-to-resource solutions
stories.summary: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and Norway's SINTEF held a dialogue on transforming industrial waste into construction resources. The initiative follows the elevation of bilateral ties to a Green Strategic Partnership in May. Both nations are focusing on circular economy practices in the construction sector.

stories.title: Ahmedabad highlights integrated urban development model
stories.summary: Ahmedabad Municipal Commissioner Banchhanidhi Pani discussed the city's approach to urban growth, citing the Sabarmati Riverfront and data-driven governance as key initiatives. The city is positioning its integrated planning as a model for addressing rapid urbanisation, climate challenges, and rising infrastructure demands across India.

stories.title: IGBC to host 24th Green Building Congress
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council will hold its 24th Green Building Congress from 26 to 28 November in Mumbai. India currently hosts over 20,620 registered green building projects covering 16.55 billion square feet. The event aims to further the country's transition toward net zero cities.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit focuses on sustainable growth
stories.summary: The Green Bengal Summit 2026 in Kolkata addressed climate-resilient urbanisation and net zero development. State Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul advocated for extending green building standards beyond Kolkata to cities including Durgapur and Siliguri. The event brought together policymakers and industry leaders to discuss future-proofing the state.

stories.title: Missing jewellery case takes turn as items found in second locker
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding gold jewellery reported missing from a former RERA chairman's bank locker has shifted. The family informed police that some of the ornaments were located in a separate bank locker. Authorities are now investigating the discrepancy in the reported missing inventory.

stories.title: Noida Authority approves maps for Sector 150 sports facilities
stories.summary: The Noida Authority has approved maps for five sports facilities within the long-delayed Sector 150 Sports City project. The plan includes a tennis center, swimming facilities, and a multipurpose hall. The move aims to revive the stalled project, which involves approximately 8,000 homebuyers.

stories.title: West Bengal to mandate rainwater harvesting for new buildings
stories.summary: West Bengal is drafting stricter wetland conservation norms and will make rainwater harvesting mandatory for new building approvals. Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul stated the government intends to replicate green building incentives, such as additional floor area ratio, in urban centers outside of Kolkata.

stories.title: Credai seeks building regulation changes in Belagavi
stories.summary: Credai has requested that the Belagavi Urban Development Authority amend master plan regulations regarding setbacks, parking, and floor area ratio. The developers also seek to align the city's high-rise classification with state standards, noting that the current 15-meter threshold differs from the state's 24-meter definition.

stories.title: Lofty releases AI index to measure time saved
stories.summary: Lofty has released an AI Index for Real Estate, which the company describes as the industry’s first tracker designed to quantify time saved by agents. Lofty claims its software completed 1.13 million tasks in October, saving agents 130,000 hours. Every AI vendor touts their own math.

stories.title: Realty of America expands into San Diego
stories.summary: Realty of America is expanding into San Diego with the addition of Zandra Ulloa and Team Z Realty. The brokerage, which has grown to more than 3,700 agents since September 2024, is bringing its agent-owned model to the Southern California market.

stories.title: Tech is changing the property search
stories.summary: Technology is reshaping the property journey for buyers and renters through increased automation and data access. Experts at the PropTech Forum in Sydney noted that while AI tools are making the process faster and more transparent, the shift also introduces new challenges for the industry.

stories.title: Housing.com promotes Priyam Sachan
stories.summary: Housing.com has appointed Priyam Sachan as senior director of marketing. Sachan, who joined the company in August 2024, previously led marketing strategy across 40 cities. He formerly held leadership roles at Zomato, Gaana and Simplilearn.

stories.title: Construction input prices remain flat
stories.summary: Construction input prices were unchanged in October as falling petroleum and lumber costs offset rising steel and copper prices. Despite the flat monthly reading, overall construction costs remain 11.5 percent higher than one year ago, according to federal data.

stories.title: Construction material prices hold steady
stories.summary: Construction input prices remained virtually unchanged in October, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. While energy and lumber costs fell, overall construction materials remain 11.5 percent more expensive than they were one year ago.

stories.title: Construction costs remain elevated
stories.summary: Construction input prices were flat in October due to lower oil and lumber costs, but remain 11.5 percent higher than last year. ABC Chief Economist Anirban Basu noted that materials impacted by tariffs, including steel and copper, are still seeing rapid price hikes.

stories.title: Building material inflation persists
stories.summary: The price index for inputs to new residential construction rose 0.3 percent in October and is 10.4 percent higher than last year. While energy prices declined, the cost of services rose 0.7 percent over the month, keeping overall inflation high for builders.

stories.title: Builders face persistent cost squeeze
stories.summary: Residential construction input costs rose 0.3 percent in October and are 10.4 percent higher than a year ago. The National Association of Home Builders noted that gains in material and service prices are offsetting energy pullbacks, leaving builders with a persistent cost squeeze.

stories.title: Builders FirstSource acquires L&P Building Supply
stories.summary: Builders FirstSource has acquired L&P Building Supply in Las Cruces, New Mexico. The deal adds to the company's existing network in the state. Managing Director John Wagner noted that merger activity remains strong in the sector despite interest-rate headwinds.

stories.title: Sandwich panel manufacturer targets industrial growth
stories.summary: Shenyang Qiangyun Color Steel and Steel Structure is promoting the use of sandwich panels for industrial and commercial construction. The company says the global industry is increasingly focused on materials that combine structural reliability with energy efficiency and installation convenience.

stories.title: P.C.C. electric poles remain standard in India
stories.summary: Prestressed cement concrete poles are the standard support for power lines across India. These poles are used for rural electrification and street lighting because they cost less than steel, do not rust and require little maintenance.

stories.title: India shotcreting market projected to grow
stories.summary: The Indian market for shotcreting equipment is expected to expand 6 to 9 percent annually through 2035. Demand is driven by infrastructure projects including tunnels and underground works, where project schedules and equipment uptime remain the primary concerns for contractors.

stories.title: CURA reports progress on cement decarbonisation
stories.summary: CURA Climate is reporting progress on electrochemical technology designed to treat limestone before it enters the cement kiln. The company says cement manufacturing accounts for 8 percent of global CO2 emissions and claims its technology could cut emissions by as much as 80 percent.

stories.title: Green Building Congress to focus on net zero
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council will host its 24th Green Building Congress in Mumbai from 26 to 28 November. The event expects over 3,000 delegates to discuss net zero buildings, green finance and sustainable urban development.

stories.title: Duchy of Cornwall builds net energy positive home
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. The Duchy of Cornwall has reportedly completed a net energy positive Biohaus home, described as a UK first. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Study questions green building labels
stories.summary: A study in Urban Science suggests that green building certifications may not guarantee safety during extreme weather events. Researchers found that current standards often focus on energy use rather than climate adaptation, leaving some buildings vulnerable to heat waves and power failures.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore receives green certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has been awarded Platinum certification under the Indian Green Building Council’s Green Campus Rating System. The institute is the first educational institution in India to receive the distinction, which recognizes campus-wide initiatives in energy efficiency, water conservation and waste management.

stories.title: Hospitality businesses face pressure to adopt ESG
stories.summary: Climate change is affecting livelihoods and ecosystems, forcing hospitality companies to reconsider operations. Sustainability has moved from a popular corporate phrase to a key business priority. Companies are now required to focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing innovative strategies to remain resilient against environmental pressures.

stories.title: India and Denmark launch green fuel technology catalogue
stories.summary: The Central Electricity Authority and the Danish Energy Agency have developed an Indian Technology Catalogue on Green Fuels. The catalogue provides a transparent information base on emerging technologies to support policymakers and investors. The initiative aims to assist India in meeting its net-zero 2070 ambition.

stories.title: US home sales drop to 2010 levels
stories.summary: Sales of previously owned U.S. homes fell 5.5% in October to an annual rate of 3.75 million, the lowest level since August 2010. Mortgage rates above 7% kept buyers on the sidelines. The decline affected all price ranges, including homes priced at $1 million and above.

stories.title: Boston Fed president defends high rates for housing
stories.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins stated that tighter monetary policy can raise housing costs in the near term but benefits the market over the long run. She argued that stable prices create predictable economic conditions. The housing market currently faces significant affordability challenges.

stories.title: Mortgage rates remain above 7 percent
stories.summary: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage fell slightly to 7.11 percent from 7.18 percent the previous week. Rates remain significantly higher than the 6.24 percent average seen a year ago. High borrowing costs continue to push both buyers and sellers to the sidelines.

stories.title: Knight Frank sees US election impact on UK housing
stories.summary: Knight Frank analysis suggests the outcome of US midterm elections could influence the UK housing market more than the recent Budget. The firm noted that potential diplomatic breakthroughs could lower inflation and borrowing costs. Political outcomes are now being weighed against local fiscal policy.
